text:
sarah (Sales): Hey team — customer (FinSolve) reached out. They want a POC with Redwood Private. Network team prefers PrivateLink but they've got a SD‑WAN edge and need predictable egress IPs for their firewall allowlist. Also asked about pricing for reserved connection vs hosted fallback. Any blockers? 

alex (Solutions): Thanks. Quick checks: PrivateLink will require an ENI in their VPC -> we give them an interface endpoint. They will need to allow inbound 443 to the endpoint and allow outbound to our NAT egress IPs if they use our outbound paths. Do they need TLS termination in their side? 

sarah (Sales): They want TLS end-to-end, we'll terminate at the model host. So only 443 outbound from customer to our endpoint. They asked about persistent source IP for auditing — SD‑WAN is NATting flows through multiple WAN hops. 

mike (NetOps): If customer needs a single egress IP, we recommend setting up a NAT gateway or a static egress device on their edge and map SD‑WAN flows through it. Alternatively, use a transit VPC with egress NAT. For PrivateLink the connection originates from their VPC -> traffic never leaves AWS public internet, but egress IPs for outbound callbacks still apply. 

jen (Security): They also sent a questionnaire: wants proof of private connectivity, TLS cert rotation policy, and a list of IPs to allow. I'll need a short IP list and a diagram. 

alex (Solutions): Here's a minimal firewall snippet they can use (customer side):

```text
# Allow traffic to Redwood PrivateLink endpoint
allow tcp from 10.0.0.0/16 to <ENI-IP> port 443

# If using our egress IPs for callbacks
allow tcp from 10.0.0.0/16 to 34.200.45.12 port 443
allow tcp from 10.0.0.0/16 to 34.200.45.13 port 443
```

alex (Solutions): Note: the 34.200.x.x egress pool is an example — we'll supply the official list for the POC. 

sarah (Sales): Pricing note from customer: they want a 30‑day POC, expected 200 rps peak, ~150k tokens/day. Which plan should we quote? 

alex (Solutions): For short POC we suggest Hosted with PrivateLink add-on. Estimate: usage + endpoint charge. Quick calc: baseline token cost + endpoint $X/day. I'll ping pricing. 

infra-bot: Created ticket #POC-1142 for egress IP allocation and price calc. 

mike (NetOps): Blocker: their SD‑WAN vendor does hairpinning; we should confirm if flows to PrivateLink stay in-region. If their egress exits a different region, endpoint will still be regional. They must either route to the same region or accept cross-region latency. 

jen (Security): Action items for us: 1) Provide official egress IP list for POC (shortlived). 2) Cert rotation policy doc. 3) Simple connectivity diagram showing PrivateLink ENI and required SG rules. I'll draft and share. 

sarah (Sales): Great. Can someone draft the one‑page connectivity + pricing summary by EOD PST? Customer wants it for their security committee tomorrow morning. 

alex (Solutions): I'll draft the connectivity + ports doc and include a small diagram. I'll also add fallback routing if they prefer VPC Peering instead. 

mike (NetOps): I'll validate the IP list and confirm cross‑region considerations. 

jen (Security): I'll add the cert rotation pointer and an excerpt from our SOC doc for the committee. 

sarah (Sales): Awesome, thanks all. I'll send interim update to customer noting those deliverables and the ticket #POC-1142. :thumbsup:
